He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn Huskies]] and was drafted by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] with the 11th pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]]. ==Early life== Bouknight grew up in [[Crown Heights, Brooklyn]], in New York City.{{cite web |last=Jacobs |first=Jeff |title=Bouknight checks all the right boxes for Hurley, Huskies |url=https://www.ctpost.com/sports/jeffjacobs/article/Jeff-Jacobs-Bouknight-checks-all-the-right-boxes-13403695.php |website=[[Connecticut Post]] |accessdate=June 21, 2020 |date=November 18, 2018}} He played [[baseball]] for much of his childhood and started playing basketball in middle school.{{cite web |last=Amore |first=Dom |title=UConn Men Notebook: James Bouknight On Campus This Weekend |url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-sp-uconn-men-recruit-james-bouknight-0915-story.html |website=[[Hartford Courant]] |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=September 14, 2018}} He began his high school career with [[La Salle Academy]] in [[Manhattan]], New York. As a junior, Bouknight averaged 17.4 points per game, leading his team to the [[2017 New York state high school boys basketball championships#Class B|New York Federation Class B state championship]], and was named tournament [[most valuable player]] (MVP).{{cite web |last=Furman |first=Andy |date=August 7, 2021 |title=Crown Heights Native James Bouknight Becomes National Name |url=https://brooklyneagle.com/articles/2021/08/07/scholastic-roundup-another-brooklynite-heads-to-the-nba |accessdate=August 6, 2023 |website=brooklyneagle.com}} He earned [[Catholic High School Athletic Association]] B Division MVP and [[New York State Sportswriters Association]] Class B Player of the Year accolades.{{cite web |last=Pietrafesa |first=Dan |title=Catholic School Leagues Honor Top Basketball Players, Coaches |url=https://www.cny.org/stories/catholic-school-leagues-honor-top-basketball-players-coaches,15190 |website=Catholic New York |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=March 1, 2017}}{{cite web |title=All-state teams in boys B, C and D basketball |url=http://newyorksportswriters.org/blog/2017-04-12-new-york-state-sportswriters-association-boys-basketball-all-state-team.shtml |publisher=[[New York State Sportswriters Association]] |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=April 12, 2017}} After the season, Bouknight [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] down and transferred to [[MacDuffie School]] in [[Granby, Massachusetts]] to gain more exposure.{{cite web |last=Cordova |first=David |title=James Bouknight: MacDuffie Scholar Improves On Offers & Introduces Division I Schools To His Game |url=https://davesjoint.net/2018/09/14/james-bouknight-macduffie-scholar-improves-on-offers-introduces-division-i-schools-to-his-game/ |publisher=Dave's Joint |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=September 14, 2018}} In his reclassified junior season, Bouknight averaged 19.3 points, five rebounds and two assists per game before suffering a season-ending [[Tear of meniscus|torn meniscus]] in his left knee. After recovering, he played for the PSA Cardinals alongside [[Cole Anthony]] on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit. As a senior, Bouknight earned All-[[New England Preparatory School Athletic Council]] AA honors.{{cite web |title=NEPSAC announces All-New England awards |url=https://newenglandrecruitingreport.com/in-the-news/nepsac-announces-all-new-england-awards |publisher=New England Recruiting Report |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=March 16, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== Bouknight was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and was considered the 53rd-best player in the 2019 class by [[247Sports]]. On September 18, 2018, before his senior season, he committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]].{{cite web |last=Finkelstein |first=Adam |title=Guard James Bouknight commits to UConn |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/24722725 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=September 18, 2018}} Bouknight chose the Huskies over offers from [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] and [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]], among others.{{cite web |title=James Bouknight |url=https://uconnhuskies.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/james-bouknight/10578 |publisher=University of Connecticut Athletics |accessdate=June 22, 2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = James Bouknight | position = [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = [[Brooklyn, NY]] | highschool = [[MacDuffie School]] (MA) | feet = 6 | inches = 4 | weight = 180 | 40 = | commitdate = September 18, 2018 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 86 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2019 | rivals ref title = UConn 2019 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2019 UConn Huskies Recruiting Class | rivals school = connecticut | scout s = | espn schoolid = 41 | 247 overall = 53 | rivals overall = 84 | espn overall = 69 | accessdate = October 21, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== On November 7, 2019, Bouknight was suspended for three games by UConn for allegedly fleeing a car crash on September 27. He had been charged with evading responsibility, interfering with a police officer, traveling too fast for conditions and operating a motor vehicle without a license.{{cite web |title=UConn's James Bouknight suspended 3 games after car crash |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28030241 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=November 7, 2019}} On February 9, 2020, Bouknight scored a freshman season-high 23 points in a 72–71 overtime win over [[2019–20 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati]]. He scored 19 points in the second half and overtime and made the two game-sealing free throws.{{cite web |last=Amore |first=Dom |title=James Bouknight becomes the go-to difference-maker and more takeaways from UConn's win over Cincinnati |url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-sp-clb-uconn-men-folo-takeaways-cincinnati-20200211-20200210-uowvuz5tf5aw5dkgepopmmlgn4-story.html |website=[[Hartford Courant]] |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=February 10, 2020}} One day later, Bouknight was named [[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) Player of the Week.{{cite web |title=Bouknight Named AAC Player Of The Week |url=https://uconnhuskies.com/news/2020/2/10/mens-basketball-bouknight-named-aac-player-of-the-week.aspx |publisher=University of Connecticut Athletics |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=February 10, 2020}} On February 29, he had his first [[double-double]] of 19 points and 10 rebounds in a 84–63 victory over [[2019–20 East Carolina Pirates men's basketball team|East Carolina]].{{cite news |title=Vital scores 27 pts., leads UConn past East Carolina, 84–63 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169494 |accessdate=June 23, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 29, 2020}} As a freshman, he averaged 13 points, 4.1 rebounds and 1.3 assists per game and was a Third Team All-AAC and All-Freshman Team selection.{{cite web |last=Amore |first=Dom |title=Christian Vital, James Bouknight represent UConn men on all-AAC teams |url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-sp-clb-uconn-notebook-all-aac-20200311-20200310-ntxlzbpzpng7nf3w3jhmymxe3e-story.html |website=[[Hartford Courant]] |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |date=March 10, 2020}} At the beginning of his sophomore season, Bouknight was named to the preseason [[John R. Wooden Award]] watch list.{{Cite web|title=Bouknight On Watch List For Wooden Award|url=https://uconnhuskies.com/news/2020/11/30/mens-basketball-bouknight-on-watch-list-for-wooden-award|access-date=2020-12-06|website=University of Connecticut Athletics|date=November 30, 2020 |language=en}} On December 20, 2020, he scored a career-high 40 points in a 76–74 overtime loss to ninth-ranked [[2020–21 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]].{{cite web |title=Bouknight Explodes for 40, But Huskies Drop Big East Opener In Overtime |url=https://uconnhuskies.com/news/2020/12/20/mens-basketball-bouknights-career-day-not-enough-as-huskies-drop-big-east-opener.aspx |website=University of Connecticut Athletics |access-date=December 21, 2020 |date=December 20, 2020}} On January 5, 2021, he suffered an elbow injury against [[2020–21 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]], and missed eight games after undergoing surgery.{{cite web |last=Amore |first=Dom |title=James Bouknight cleared to rejoin UConn men for game against Providence Tuesday |url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-sp-uconn-men-james-bouknight-injury-20210216-20210216-sgjfwlycqbfqfnycgd4d7by4gy-story.html |website=[[Hartford Courant]] |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=February 16, 2021}} As a sophomore, he averaged 18.7 points and 5.7 rebounds per game, earning First Team All-[[Big East Conference|Big East]] honors. On March 31, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |authorlink=Adrian Wojnarowski |title=UConn Huskies' James Bouknight entering 2021 NBA draft, will hire agent |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31172084 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=March 31, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Charlotte Hornets / Greensboro Swarm (2021–2024)=== Bouknight was selected with the 11th pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite news|first=Steve|last=Reed|title=Hornets get Bouknight at No. 11, Jones at No. 19 via Knicks|url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-nba-nba-draft-detroit-pistons-charlotte-hornets-cf2da2655d5f5e6856b52b109c0e7c65|work=[[Associated Press]]|date=July 30, 2021|access-date=July 30, 2021}} On August 3, 2021, he officially signed with the Hornets.{{cite web|first=Quinton|last=Wash|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign James Bouknight and Kai Jones|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/charlotte-hornets-sign-james-bouknight-and-kai-jones|work=NBA.com|date=August 3, 2021|access-date=August 4, 2021}} Bouknight made his NBA debut on October 22, 2021, in a 123–112 victory against the [[2021–22 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]], getting only one rebound on a minute of playing time.{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets vs Cleveland Cavaliers Oct 22, 2021 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/game/cha-vs-cle-0022100017/box-score|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 1, 2022}} He scored his first NBA points on November 26, in a 133–115 victory over the [[2021–22 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]], scoring two free throws in four minutes.{{cite web|title=Minnesota Timberwolves vs Charlotte Hornets Nov 26, 2021 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/game/min-vs-cha-0022100281/box-score|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 1, 2022}} On December 10, Bouknight scored a career-high 24 points in a 124–123 win over the [[2021–22 Sacramento Kings season|Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|title=Game Recap: Hornets 124, Kings 123|url=https://www.nba.com/watch/video/game-recap-hornets-124-kings-123-zj4fkf|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 1, 2022}} Prior to the 2022–23 season, Bouknight changed his jersey number from 5 to 2.{{cite web|first=Schuyler|last=Callihan|title=James Bouknight to Switch Jersey Numbers?|url=https://www.si.com/nba/hornets/news/james-bouknight-to-switch-jersey-numbers|website=SI.com|date=July 22, 2022 |access-date=October 1, 2022}} On February 8, 2024, Bouknight was waived by the Hornets.{{cite web|title=Hornets Waive James Bouknight, Frank Ntilikina And Ish Smith|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-waive-james-bouknight-frank-ntilikina-and-ish-smith|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}} ===Rip City Remix (2024–present)=== On October 15, 2024, Bouknight signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]],{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign James Bouknight to Exhibit 10 Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-james-bouknight-to-exhibit-10-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2024|access-date=October 15, 2024}} but was waived the next day.{{cite tweet|author=Portland Trail Blazers|title=The Portland Trail Blazers have waived guard James Bouknight.|number=1846595900271219024|user=trailblazers|date=October 16, 2024|access-date=October 18, 2024}} On October 28, he joined the [[Rip City Remix]].{{cite tweet|author=Rip City Remix|title=Your official 2024 Remix training camp roster 🫨💿|number=1850928196042346714|user=ripcityremix|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 4, 2024}} Bouknight joined the Trail Blazers for the [[2025 NBA Summer League]]. ==Personal life== ===Legal issues=== On October 16, 2022, Bouknight was arrested by [[Charlotte-Mecklenburg Police Department|Charlotte-Mecklenburg Police]] for [[driving while intoxicated]] at around 1:51 a.m. He was found [[Binge drinking|unconscious]] in a parking deck around 12:44 a.m. At the time of his arrest, he had a .40-caliber gun, a [[Glock 23]], and a bag of Doritos.{{Cite web |date=2022-10-17 |title=NBA's James Bouknight Arrested For Driving While Impaired |url=https://www.tmz.com/2022/10/17/nba-james-bouknight-arrested-driving-while-impaired/ |access-date=2022-10-18 |website=TMZ |language=en}}https://nypost.com/2022/10/19/hornets-james-bouknight-was-asleep-with-gun-doritos-before-dwi/ His bond was set at $2,500, and he returned to practice the following day. Prior to this incident, he had multiple speeding and reckless driving offenses.{{Cite web |last1=Cox |first1=Kallie |last2=Boone |first2=Roderick |date=October 17, 2022 |title=James Bouknight arrested on impaired driving charge in Charlotte |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/charlotte-hornets/article267431857.html |website=Charlotte Observer}} He was sentenced to a year of probation.{{cite web | url=https://www.wsoctv.com/news/local/former-hornets-guard-james-bouknight-sentenced-dwi/Y6WSO6JP2VFVFJTGYCYGF6JDPA/ | title=Former Hornets' guard James Bouknight sentenced for
